purpose: Synthetic functional control only. It tests whether the Attack Feasibility critic can emit opposite directional stances when supplied modality-matched directional evidence. It is not part of the seven empirical evaluation cases and must not be pooled with empirical results.

claims.statement: The supplied evidence reports that, under unchanged reporting coverage, DDoS incidents increased from 100 in 2022 to 130 in 2023 and to 160 in 2024, reporting incident count/frequency only.
The supplied record is expressly a synthetic functional-control record and not empirical evidence.
The supplied record permits directional threat trend claims and prohibits claims about attack magnitude, attack severity, tactic prevalence, and causal attribution.

stance_basis.rationale: The only directional evidence in the payload explicitly reports an increasing DDoS incident count/frequency through 2024, which directly matches the forecasted NoI threat state direction. No supplied evidence contradicts that directional threat trend, although the evidence base is synthetic, partial, and does not establish attack magnitude, severity, causal drivers, or post-2024 outcomes.

unresolved_questions: Whether the synthetic functional-control trend corresponds to independent empirical DDoS incident-count trends after the 2024-12-31 cutoff.
